Finish with the five points on importance, drawing out how consequences spread beyond the person attacked. Then set the exercise questions.

units.title: Application Packages
units.overview: Hands-on use of an office suite — word processing, spreadsheets, presentations and a simple database — plus an introduction to software written for one particular job.
units.summary: A word processor produces documents, a spreadsheet works with numbers in cells and formulas, presentation software builds slide shows, and a database stores records. Domain-specific tools are built for one trade.

detailed.heading: Chapter 11 — Application Packages
detailed.note: Notes for Chapter 11 of the Class 8 book: the office package — the word processor, the spreadsheet, the presentation tool and the database management system — followed by domain-specific tools.
learning_objectives: Create and format a document in a word processor
Use formulas and functions in a spreadsheet
Build a slide presentation
Store and retrieve records in a simple database

blocks.text: Nearly every office, school and business needs the same handful of things done: letters written, numbers added up, talks illustrated, records kept. An office package is the answer to that — several programs, sold and installed together, that share a common look and can pass work between one another.
A group of programs designed to help users perform everyday tasks in offices, schools and businesses — writing documents, calculating data, creating presentations, and managing emails and databases.

The four applications this chapter covers are the word processor (MS Word), the spreadsheet package (MS Excel), the presentation tool (MS PowerPoint) and the database management system (MS Access). Each is described below, and the chapter closes with domain-specific tools — software written for one particular kind of work.

blocks.title: Exam note
blocks.text: The four extensions are worth learning by heart. The older three-letter forms (.doc, .xls, .ppt) belong to versions up to 2003; from 2007 onwards an "x" was added.

Software that lets users type and manage documents — letters, reports, assignments and résumés — in digital form. It creates documents through computerised text editing, formatting, storing and printing.

What it really changes is the cost of a mistake. On paper, rewriting a paragraph means rewriting the page. In a word processor you correct the word and the page reflows itself. That, plus the ability to make text look right, is the whole of it.
What it is used for
Résumés and bio-data, cover letters, advertisements, reports, blog entries and web pages, newsletters, annual reports, articles, directories, brochures, and books.
Popular word processing packages
MS Word, WordStar, Lotus Word Pro, WordPerfect, MS Write, Kingsoft Writer, Professional Write, Apache OpenOffice Writer, AmiPro, Lotus Notes, MultiMate and Ted.
MS Word
Microsoft Word is the most widely used of them, and it is what the rest of this section describes. It is part of the Microsoft Office package and is used to create, edit, format and print documents.

It offers every word processing facility you would expect: creating, editing, formatting, saving and printing; checking spelling and grammar; finding synonyms and antonyms through a thesaurus; newspaper columns; tables; footnotes and endnotes; page numbers; special symbols; bookmarks and comments; and inserting pictures and objects such as video clips, audio clips, PowerPoint presentations, equations and AutoCAD drawings. It can also build a table of contents and an index.
Its extension is .docx. The older .doc was used up to MS Word 2003.
Opening MS Word
Click Start, then choose Microsoft Word. Or press the Windows key with R, type WinWord into the Run box, and press Enter.
Working with documents

items: Save — Ctrl+S. To keep the original and save a copy under a new name, use Save As. To produce a file another program can read, use Save as type and pick the format.
Open — Ctrl+O.
Select text — drag across it; Ctrl+A selects the whole document.
Format text — bold (Ctrl+B), italic (Ctrl+I), underline (Ctrl+U), superscript (Ctrl+Shift+=) and subscript (Ctrl+=), colour, effects, styles, Format Painter and WordArt.
Align paragraphs — left (Ctrl+L), centre (Ctrl+E), right (Ctrl+R) and justified (Ctrl+J).
Lists and spacing — bulleted and numbered lists, multilevel lists, line spacing (single, 1.5 and double) and space before or after a paragraph.
Edit — copy (Ctrl+C), cut (Ctrl+X), paste (Ctrl+V), undo (Ctrl+Z), redo (Ctrl+Y), find (Ctrl+F) and replace (Ctrl+H).
Check the writing — Spelling and Grammar, AutoCorrect, and the Thesaurus for a better word.
Tables — insert a table, add or delete rows and columns, and merge or split cells.
Pictures — insert a picture from a file, then position and resize it.

Page furniture — page numbers, page and section breaks, headers and footers (including removing them from the first page), watermarks, page colour and page borders, page margins and page orientation, print preview and printing.
Extras — shapes and SmartArt, equations, symbols and special characters, and mail merge for sending the same letter to many people.

blocks.text: Mail merge
Mail merge takes one document and one list of people and produces one personalised copy for each. It runs in four stages.

items: Set up the main document — the letter as it will go out, with placeholders where names go.
Connect to a data source — the list of recipients, usually a spreadsheet or a table.
Insert the merge fields — the address block and the greeting line.
Preview and finish — preview the merge, adjust individual copies if needed, then print them.

blocks.text: Shortcut keys

blocks.title: Exam note
blocks.text: Two pairs catch people out. Ctrl+Shift+= is superscript and Ctrl+= is subscript — the one with Shift is the one that goes up. And Ctrl+M is a paragraph indent in Word but a new slide in PowerPoint, so learn each in its program.

A spreadsheet is the tool you reach for once numbers are involved: a sales bill, a salary sheet, a mark sheet, a budget, an income statement, a balance sheet. Its real power is not that it adds up — it is that when you change one number, every figure that depended on it changes too.
Microsoft Excel is the best-known spreadsheet, and it is what this section describes. Its file is called a workbook and ends in .xlsx; the older .xls was used up to Excel 2003.
What a spreadsheet is used for

items: Basic mathematical calculation, financial modelling and analysis, statistical analysis, and scientific and engineering calculation.
Database management, graphic presentation, and a front end to a database.
Custom applications built with Visual Basic for Applications (VBA).
Everyday documents: bills and vouchers, salary sheets, income and expense statements, balance sheets, budgets and grade calculations.

blocks.text: Features of a spreadsheet

items: Data entry, storage, calculation and presentation.
Formatting — font, font colour, font size and borders.
Simple operations: copy, cut, paste, find and replace.
Sorting data ascending or descending on any field.
Formulas using cell addresses, covering mathematical, statistical and trigonometric work.
Shared workbooks — several people editing the same file at once.
Charts in many types: pie, bar, XY, stacked bar, area and 3D pie.
Data validation, to set rules for what may be entered.
Internet features — a web toolbar, hyperlinks, and saving as HTML.
Advanced tools: goal seek, scenarios, auditing, what-if analysis, pivot tables and pivot charts.
Object linking and embedding, so data moves safely between Word and Excel.
Natural language formulas.

blocks.text: The basics: workbook, worksheet, cell

head: Term
What it is
rows: The file you work in and store data in. It contains worksheets — three by default.

An electronic sheet: a grid of vertical columns and horizontal rows, like an account sheet or a mark sheet. In Excel 2016 it has 1,048,576 rows and 16,384 columns; Excel 2003 had 65,536 rows and 256 columns. The numbers differ from package to package.
The intersection of a row and a column, where data is stored. Cells are outlined by light grey gridlines. A cell holds up to 32,000 characters.
The cell you are working in, shown by a thick black border. Its reference appears in the Name Box, left of the formula bar.
A block of cells, written first cell to last — for example A1:E15.

blocks.text: Cell reference

A cell's location is its cell reference: the column letter and the row number, with the letter first — A1, B3, Z345. References matter most in formulas: rather than writing =3+2, you write =A1+A2, so the answer follows the cells rather than the numbers you first typed.
There are three kinds, and the difference shows itself when you copy a formula to another cell.

head: Type
Written as
What happens when copied
rows: Changes to reflect the new position. This is the default.
Stays fixed on that cell. Press F4 to add the dollar signs.
$A1 fixes the column and lets the row move; A$1 fixes the row and lets the column move.

blocks.title: Exam note
blocks.text: The dollar sign is what pins a reference down: whatever it stands in front of does not move. $C$4 pins both, $C4 pins the column, C$4 pins the row, and plain C4 pins nothing.
Types of data

head: Type
What it covers
rows: Any combination of letters, numbers and special characters — up to 32,000 characters
An error value produced by a formula or function

blocks.text: Operators
An operator is the symbol that says what to do between two operands — in 4+5, the 4 and 5 are operands and the + is the operator.

head: Group
Operators
Meaning
rows: Addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, exponent — for example 2^3 is 8
Compare two values; the result is TRUE or FALSE
AND is TRUE only if every condition is TRUE; OR is TRUE if any one is; NOT reverses its argument
A colon spans all cells between two, as in A2:A7; a comma combines references, as in SUM(A1,A2,A3)

blocks.text: Formulas and their rules
A sequence of values, cell references and operators that produces a new value from existing ones.

items: A formula must begin with an equal sign, =.
Press Enter to confirm it.
Formulas are not case sensitive — =A1+B1 and =a1+b1 are the same.
A formula may contain numbers, cell references, constants, operators and functions.

blocks.text: Functions
A readymade formula built into Excel. Functions let you do a calculation quickly without spelling out every step.

head: Function
What it does
Syntax
rows: Adds all the numbers in a range
Multiplies all the numbers in a range
Returns the serial number of the current date
Returns the serial number of the current date and time
Returns the serial number for a particular date

blocks.text: Conditional formulas: the IF function
IF lets a cell decide between two answers. It takes three arguments.

head: Argument
What it is
rows: What to return if the condition is true
What to return if the condition is false

blocks.text: So =IF(D2>=25000, 5%*D2, 10%*D2) gives 5% of D2 when D2 is at least 25,000, and 10% otherwise. Conditions can be combined with AND (TRUE only if every condition is TRUE), OR (TRUE if any one is) and NOT (reverses its argument).

IF functions can also be nested, one inside another, to sort a value into several bands — for example returning "First" above 60%, "Second" from 50 to 60%, "Third" from 40 to 50%, and "***" below that.
Charts
A graphical presentation of numeric data from the worksheet. Change the data and the chart updates itself. Excel offers column, line, pie, bar, area and scatter charts.

head: Component
What it is
rows: The chart's title, typed in or taken from a worksheet cell
The mark that distinguishes one data series from another
Show the actual value of each data point
Small lines dividing the axes and providing the scale
The category axis — the categories plotted
The series or rank axis — the values plotted
Lines making the value of each point easier to read

blocks.text: Page setup and printing
Set the page margins and orientation, use Print Preview from the File tab to see how the sheet will look, then choose the printer, the number of copies and the other settings before printing.

The practice of showing and explaining the content of a topic to an audience. A presentation helps both sides: the speaker gets easier access to their ideas, and the audience gets visual information that supports the talk.

Presentation software has largely replaced pamphlets, handouts, chalkboards, flip charts, posters, slides and overhead transparencies. Text, graphics, movies and other objects are placed on individual pages, called slides, which can be printed or — more usually — shown on screen and moved through at the speaker's command.
What a presentation program does
Every presentation program provides the same three things, plus the fourth that ties them together:

items: An editor for inserting and formatting text.
A way to insert and manipulate graphic images.
A slide-show system to display the content.
Tools to design slides, format them, set animation and sound, set effects, and display the result.

blocks.text: Examples: MS PowerPoint, Apple Keynote, OpenOffice.org Impress, KPresenter, Corel Presentations, MagicPoint, IBM Lotus Freelance Graphics, Harvard Graphics, Simple Slides, Powerdot and Opera Show Format.
Features of a presentation package

items: Data entry, storage, calculation and presentation.
Formatting with font, font colour and font size.
Copy, cut, paste, find and replace.
Pre-designed slide designs for faster development.
Slide transition, defining how one slide gives way to the next.
Predefined slide animation, and custom animation of your own.
Navigation buttons for moving between slides.
Bookmarks and hyperlinks to link parts of a presentation.
Chart types — pie, bar, XY, stacked bar, area and 3D pie.
Internet features: a web toolbar, hyperlinks, and saving as HTML.

blocks.text: The basics: slide, animation, transition

head: Term
What it is
rows: A single page of a presentation. A presentation is made of several slides.
A visual effect applied to individual items on a slide — graphics, titles or bullet points.
The visual movement as one slide changes to the next.

blocks.title: The difference that matters
blocks.text: Animation moves the objects on a slide. Transition moves the whole slide. If you can remember that one sentence, you have the distinction.
The three slide views

head: View
What it is for
rows: The main editing view, where you write and design. It has three areas: tabs on the left alternating between an outline and slide thumbnails; the slide pane on the right; and the notes pane at the bottom.
All your slides as thumbnails on one screen. Use it when the presentation is nearly finished, to reorder, add or delete slides and to preview transitions and animations.
Full screen, the way the audience will see it — graphics, timings, movies, animation and transitions all as they will appear. Press F5 to start.

blocks.text: Building a presentation in PowerPoint

items: Start it from Start › Programs › Microsoft PowerPoint, or run powerpnt.
Work with text boxes — resize them, move them, give them a background colour, and delete them.
Add and duplicate slides — Ctrl+M inserts a new slide.
Apply a theme — Office themes give the whole deck a consistent look at once.
Insert content — pictures, shapes, SmartArt, tables, charts with editable data, and video and audio clips. (Both sound and movie clips can be inserted.)
Set transitions and animations from the Transitions and Animation tabs, using Preview to check them.
Set up the show — run from the beginning, or from the current slide.
Print — choose full-page slides, handouts (2, 3, 4, 6 or 9 slides to a page), notes pages with the speaker's notes, or the outline view.

blocks.text: The PowerPoint file ends in .pptx; the older .ppt was used up to PowerPoint 2003.
A collection of related information about a subject, organised in a useful manner so that it provides a base for retrieving information, drawing conclusions and making decisions.

A set of programs that manages the database files. It allows access to the files, updating of records, and retrieval of data on request. It acts as the interface between the application program and the data in the database.
Examples: Microsoft Access, Oracle, MySQL, SQL Server, dBase and FoxPro.
Uses of a DBMS

items: Storing data.
Accessing data when it is needed.
Updating and modifying data.
Deleting or removing data.
Providing security, so that only authorised people can use the data.
Sharing data for concurrent access.
Maintaining the accuracy of the data.
Enforcing standards or rules for accessing the data.
Reducing data redundancy.
Providing timely and accurate information.

blocks.text: MS Access

Microsoft Access is a multi-user relational database management system (RDBMS). It stores and manipulates large amounts of information and performs repetitive tasks, and it keeps an entire database application in a single file with the .accdb extension.
Although the word "database" usually means a collection of related tables, an Access file holds more than data. It contains four kinds of object.

head: Object
What it does
rows: Store the data in the database.
Ask questions about information stored in the tables, and fetch the data you need.
Let you view and insert data into the tables on screen.
Print data based on queries and tables.

blocks.title: Exam note
blocks.text: The four objects are easy to confuse, so pair each with its verb: tables store, queries ask, forms enter, reports print.
Application software developed and used for one particular domain or area, built to meet the requirements of that domain.
Where Word and Excel are general-purpose, these programs are built for one job — running a school, tracking stock, paying staff. The chapter looks at six.
School Management System

An information system that records data, manages transactions and generates reports for a school, automating its operations. It supports students and teachers and improves the administration of the school as a whole.

It usually handles: student information (attendance, homework, discipline, grades, achievements); parent access; teacher information; communication (voice messaging, email, chat); attendance and timetable management; online classes, assessments and assignments; report card generation; fee tracking and online payment; admission management; profiles of students, teachers, staff and parents; library management; transport management; and hostel management.
Inventory Management System

Inventory is the list of stock items held for trading or consumption — raw materials, work in process, finished goods and consumables. An inventory management system records and manages every transaction involving them: it tracks inventory levels, orders, sales and deliveries. In manufacturing it also raises work orders, bills of materials and other production documents.
Features: inventory management; inventory tracking and barcoding; reporting tools; inventory forecasting; and inventory alerts.
Payroll System
Payroll is the process by which employers pay employees for work completed — salary and wages. A payroll management system organises everything to do with employee payment and tax filing.

Features: tracking the job done; calculating wages and salary; tracking attendance; recording and managing leave; withholding taxes and deductions; printing and delivering cheques; completing direct deposits; and paying employment taxes to the government.
Financial Accounting System
Software used to record and process accounting transactions. It normally contains accounts payable, accounts receivable, journal, general ledger, payroll and trial balance modules.

Features: tracking the flow of financial data across the organisation in a controlled manner and integrating it for strategic decision making; creation of organisational structure; general ledger accounting (chart of accounts, account groups, data transfer rules, general ledger accounts); tax and configuration; account payables; account receivables; asset accounting; and integration with sales and distribution and materials management.
Hotel Management System
A system for running hotels, hostels, lodges, suites, resorts and other rental properties. It handles day-to-day operations and administration, booking and billing, and helps guests be served well.

Features: billing operations; booking and reservations; detailed reporting; housekeeping management; detailed guest history; banquet management; human resource management; inventory management; and customer relationship management.
Weather Forecasting System
A tool for predicting the weather or climatic conditions at a future time for a given location — cloud cover, rain, snow, wind speed and temperature before they happen.

Forecasts are made by collecting as much data as possible about the current state of the atmosphere — particularly temperature, humidity and wind — and using meteorology to work out how it will evolve. Because the atmosphere is complex and not fully understood, forecasts become less accurate the further ahead they look.

The main methods used are: looking at current weather conditions; tracking the motion of air and clouds in the sky; finding previous weather patterns that resemble current ones; examining changes in air pressure; and running computer models.

short.question: What do you understand by formatting a document? Give the significance of speller and thesaurus of a modern word processing package.
short.answer:
Formatting a document means changing how it looks without changing what it says: font, size, colour, bold and italic, alignment, line and paragraph spacing, bullets and numbering, borders and shading, headers and footers, and page setup. The words stay the same; the presentation changes, and that is often what decides whether anyone reads it.

The speller checks words against a dictionary and flags the ones it does not know, so typing mistakes get caught before the document goes out. The thesaurus offers synonyms and antonyms, which helps you pick a better or more exact word. Together they do two different jobs: the speller guards correctness, the thesaurus improves style.

short.question: Explain briefly about document formatting in a word processing package.
short.answer:
Document formatting covers everything that governs the appearance of a document rather than its content. It works at three levels.

  • Character formatting — font, size, colour, bold, italic, underline, superscript, subscript, effects and styles.
  • Paragraph formatting — alignment (left, centre, right, justified), indentation, line spacing, space before and after, and bullets or numbering.
  • Page formatting — margins, orientation, size, page colour and borders, headers and footers, page numbers, page and section breaks, and watermarks.

Styles tie it together: a named bundle of settings you can apply to many places at once and then change everywhere by editing the style once.

short.question: Explain the following terms used in different software packages: (a) Cut and paste (b) Text justification.
short.answer:
(a) Cut and paste. Cut removes the selected text from the document and holds it on the clipboard (Ctrl+X); paste puts it somewhere else (Ctrl+V). Copy (Ctrl+C) does the same but leaves the original in place. So cut moves text and copy duplicates it — both then use paste.

(b) Text justification. Justified text is stretched so that both the left and right edges line up evenly, giving a clean block like a newspaper column (Ctrl+J). It differs from the other alignments: left-aligned has a ragged right edge, right-aligned a ragged left edge, and centred is evenly ragged on both sides.

short.question: What do you mean by word processing? Distinguish between word processing and data processing software.
short.answer:
Word processing is creating, editing, formatting, storing and printing text documents with a computer — letters, reports, assignments and résumés — so that corrections can be made without retyping the whole page.

BasisWord processingData processing
Works onText — words and sentencesNumbers and records
Main jobWriting, formatting and laying out documentsCalculating, sorting and summarising data
ResultA readable documentFigures, totals, reports
Typical programMS WordMS Excel, MS Access
What matters mostAppearance and clarityAccuracy and consistency

A letter is word processing; the class mark sheet it refers to is data processing.

short.question: What is a word processor? State the advantages of the word processor in document designing.
short.answer:
A word processor is software that lets you type and manage documents digitally — creating them through computerised text editing, formatting, storing and printing.

Advantages in document design:

  • Corrections are free. Change a word and the page reflows; nothing has to be retyped.
  • Everything looks consistent. Styles apply one set of settings across the whole document, and Format Painter copies formatting from one place to another.
  • Layout is easy. Margins, orientation, columns, headers, footers and page numbers are set in moments.
  • Pictures and objects fit in. Images, shapes, SmartArt, tables, charts and equations all sit inside the text.
  • Writing improves. Spelling and grammar checking, AutoCorrect and a thesaurus are all built in.
  • Work can be reused. Templates, saved styles and mail merge mean the second document takes a fraction of the time of the first.

short.question: Explain the features of a word processor.
short.answer:
A word processor offers all of the following.

  • Creating, editing, saving and printing documents.
  • Formatting text — font, size, colour, bold, italic, underline, superscript and subscript, effects, styles and Format Painter.
  • Formatting paragraphs — alignment, indentation, line and paragraph spacing, bullets and numbering.
  • Editing tools — copy, cut, paste, undo, redo, find and replace; select all, word, line or paragraph.
  • Checking the writing — spelling and grammar, AutoCorrect, thesaurus for synonyms and antonyms.
  • Tables — inserting them, adding and deleting rows and columns, merging and splitting cells, borders and shading.
  • Objects — pictures, shapes, SmartArt, WordArt, equations, symbols and special characters, hyperlinks, bookmarks and comments.
  • Page features — margins, orientation, page and section breaks, headers and footers, page numbers, watermarks, page colour and borders, columns, drop caps, footnotes and endnotes.
  • Long documents — table of contents and index.
  • Mail merge, for one letter to many recipients.
  • Print preview and printing.

short.question: What is a word processor? List the major features of a word processor.
short.answer:
A word processor is application software for creating and managing text documents in digital form — letters, reports, assignments and résumés — by editing, formatting, storing and printing them. MS Word is the best-known example; its files end in .docx.

The features that matter most:

  1. Editing without retyping — insert, delete, move and copy text freely.
  2. Formatting — character, paragraph and page.
  3. Styles and templates — consistent design applied across a document or reused between documents.
  4. Spelling, grammar and thesaurus.
  5. Tables and columns.
  6. Inserting pictures and objects — images, shapes, charts, equations and symbols.
  7. Page setup — margins, orientation, headers, footers, page numbers and watermarks.
  8. Mail merge — one document sent to many recipients.
  9. Saving in other formats, and printing with preview.

short.question: Explain briefly about cell referencing in a spreadsheet package.
short.answer:
A cell reference is a cell's location, written as the column letter followed by the row number — A1, B3, Z345. It matters most in formulas: instead of =3+2 you write =A1+A2, so the result follows whatever is in those cells rather than the numbers you happened to type when you wrote it.

There are three kinds.

TypeWrittenWhen copied
RelativeC4Shifts to match the new position — the default
Absolute$C$4Stays on that cell; press F4 to add the dollar signs
Mixed$A1 or A$1$A1 fixes the column; A$1 fixes the row

The dollar sign pins down whatever it stands before — column or row.

short.question: What is a spreadsheet package? State the advantages of the spreadsheet package.
short.answer:
A spreadsheet package is application software that stores data in a grid of rows and columns and performs calculations on it. MS Excel is the best-known example; its file is a workbook ending in .xlsx.

Advantages:

  • Answers follow the data. Change a number and every formula depending on it updates at once — no recalculating and no arithmetic slip.
  • Built-in functions. SUM, AVERAGE, MAX, MIN, COUNT and the rest do in one word what would otherwise be a long formula.
  • What-if analysis. Try a different figure and see the consequence immediately — the whole point of goal seek and scenarios.
  • Charts come free. Numbers become pictures with a few clicks, and they keep up with the data.
  • Data can be managed. Sorting, filtering and validation keep large sets in order.
  • Work is shareable. Several people can edit the same workbook, and the data links safely to and from Word.

short.question: Explain the main features of a spreadsheet package.
short.answer:
• Grid layout — worksheets of rows and columns, grouped into a workbook.
  • Data entry and four data types — text, numbers, logical values and errors.
  • Formulas and functions using cell references, with relative, absolute and mixed addressing.
  • Operators — arithmetic, relational, logical and reference.
  • Conditional logic through IF, AND, OR and NOT.
  • Formatting — font, colour, size, borders, number formats and conditional formatting.
  • Data tools — sorting, filtering, validation, AutoFill.
  • Charts — pie, bar, line, area, scatter, XY, stacked and 3D types.
  • Sharing — several users editing one workbook at once.
  • Advanced analysis — goal seek, scenarios, auditing, what-if analysis, pivot tables and pivot charts.
  • Integration — object linking and embedding with Word, plus web features and saving as HTML.

short.question: What is an application program? List the major features of the spreadsheet.
short.answer:
An application program is software written to do a particular job for the person using it — writing letters, calculating accounts, showing slides — as distinct from system software, which runs the computer itself. Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Access are all application programs.

Major features of a spreadsheet:

  1. Worksheets of rows and columns inside a workbook.
  2. Cells holding text, numbers, logical values or errors.
  3. Cell references — relative, absolute and mixed.
  4. Formulas beginning with =, and built-in functions such as SUM, AVERAGE, MAX, MIN, COUNT and SQRT.
  5. Arithmetic, relational, logical and reference operators.
  6. Conditional formulas with IF, AND, OR and NOT.
  7. Formatting, including conditional formatting.
  8. Sorting, filtering, validation and AutoFill.
  9. Charts of many types.
  10. Page setup, print preview and printing.

short.question: Write short notes on: (a) Cell (b) Goal seek (c) Conditional formatting (d) What-if analysis.
short.answer:
(a) Cell. The intersection of a row and a column in a worksheet, where data is stored. Cells are outlined by light grey gridlines and are named by column letter then row number — A1 is the first. The cell you are working in is the active cell, with a thick border and its reference in the Name Box. A cell holds up to 32,000 characters.

(b) Goal seek. Working backwards. Instead of asking what a formula produces, you say what answer you want and Excel works out which input gives it. If a loan repayment must stay under Rs. 10,000 a month, goal seek finds the largest amount you can borrow.

(c) Conditional formatting. Formatting that applies only when a condition holds — every number below 40 shown in red, for instance. Because it is a rule rather than a one-off colouring, it follows the data: fix the figure and the colour changes by itself.

(d) What-if analysis. Changing inputs to see what happens to the results — testing a budget at 5% inflation, then at 10%. Goal seek, scenarios and data tables are all forms of it. It is the main reason spreadsheets are used for planning rather than only for recording.

short.question: What is a presentation package? Explain with its features.
short.answer:
A presentation package is application software used to show information, usually as a slide show. It normally provides three things: an editor for inserting and formatting text; a way to insert and manipulate graphic images; and a slide-show system to display the content. On top of that it lets you create slides, design and format them, set animation and sound, set effects, and display the result. MS PowerPoint is the best-known example; its files end in .pptx.

Features:

  • Data entry, storage, calculation and presentation.
  • Formatting — font, font colour, font size.
  • Copy, cut, paste, find and replace.
  • Pre-designed slide designs for faster work.
  • Slide transition, setting how one slide gives way to the next.
  • Predefined and custom animation.
  • Navigation buttons between slides.
  • Bookmarks and hyperlinks linking parts of a presentation.
  • Charts — pie, bar, XY, stacked bar, area and 3D pie.
  • Web features: a web toolbar, hyperlinks, and saving as HTML.
  • Printing as full-page slides, handouts, notes pages or outlines.

short.question: Define the terms 'animation', 'slide transition' and 'slide design' in the context of a presentation package.
short.answer:
Animation. A visual effect applied to individual items on a slide — graphics, titles or bullet points. It is a simulation of movement made by displaying a series of pictures or frames, and it controls when and how each object appears.

Slide transition. The visual movement as one slide changes to the next. It governs the movement of the whole slide, whereas animation moves the objects on it — that is the difference to remember.

Slide design. The overall look of the slides — background, colour scheme, fonts and layout. A theme applies one design across the whole presentation at once, which is what keeps a deck consistent and is why starting from a theme beats designing slide by slide.

short.question: Write short notes on: (a) Slide (b) Custom animation.
short.answer:
(a) Slide. A single page of a presentation, created with software such as PowerPoint or OpenOffice Impress. A presentation is made up of several slides, each holding text, graphics, movies or other objects. Slides can be printed or, more usually, shown on screen and moved through at the speaker's command.

(b) Custom animation. Animation you define yourself, rather than taking one of the built-in presets. You choose which object is affected, what effect it uses, when it starts, how long it runs, and in what order it appears against the other objects on the slide. It is how you make a bullet list appear point by point as you speak, instead of all at once when the slide arrives. The Animation tab's Preview button lets you check the result.

short.question: What is a Database Management System?
short.answer:
A Database Management System (DBMS) is a set of programs that manages database files. It allows access to the files, updating of records, and retrieval of data as requested.

Its role is to sit between the application program and the data itself, so the program asks the DBMS for what it needs and never has to deal with how the data is physically stored.

Examples: Microsoft Access, Oracle, MySQL, SQL Server, dBase and FoxPro.

short.question: List out the uses of a DBMS.
short.answer:
1. Storing data.
  2. Accessing data when it is required.
  3. Updating and modifying data.
  4. Deleting or removing data.
  5. Providing security, so that data can be used only by authorised people.
  6. Sharing data for concurrent access.
  7. Maintaining the accuracy of the data.
  8. Enforcing standards or rules for accessing the data.
  9. Reducing data redundancy.
  10. Providing timely and accurate information.

short.question: Define MS-Access.
short.answer:
Microsoft Access is a powerful multi-user relational database management system (RDBMS) developed by Microsoft. It is used to store and manipulate large amounts of information and to perform repetitive tasks.

It builds desktop and client/server database applications that run under Windows, and it keeps an entire database application in a single file with the .accdb extension. That file can hold data objects — tables, indexes and queries — and application objects — forms, reports, macros and Visual Basic code.

short.question: Define queries.
short.answer:
A query is a question asked of the information stored in the tables. It is the means of getting the particular data you need out of a database.

Instead of opening a table and hunting through every row, you state what you are looking for — every student in class 8 with attendance below 80%, say — and the query returns just those records. Queries are also what forms and reports are usually built on, which is why they sit at the centre of how a database is used.

short.question: Differentiate between data and information.
short.answer:
Data is raw, unprocessed facts with no meaning of their own. Information is data that has been processed, organised and given meaning, so that it is useful for making a decision.

The marks 65, 70 and 75 are data. The statement that the class average is 70 is information.

BasisDataInformation
StateRaw, unprocessed factsProcessed and meaningful
MeaningLittle on its ownClear and purposeful
Depends onNothing — it is the inputData, after processing
UseFeeds into processingSupports decisions
Example65, 70, 75Average = 70

short.question: Explain the school management system with its desirable features.
short.answer:
A School Management System is an information system that records data, manages transactions and generates reports for a school. It automates the school's operations, supports students and teachers, and improves the administration of the school as a whole.

Desirable features:

  1. Student information — attendance, homework, discipline, grades and achievements.
  2. Parent access, so that parents and guardians can see their child's information.
  3. Teacher information — activities, class timings, student progress and classroom activities.
  4. Communication — voice messaging, email and chat.
  5. Attendance and timetable management.
  6. Online classes, assessments and assignments.
  7. Report card generation.
  8. Fee tracking and online payment.
  9. Admission management.
  10. Profile management for students, teachers, staff and parents.
  11. Library management.
  12. Transport management.
  13. Hostel management.

short.question: What is the financial accounting system? What are its uses?
short.answer:
Financial accounting software is used to record and process accounting transactions. It normally contains modules for accounts payable, accounts receivable, journal, general ledger, payroll and trial balance.

Features and uses:

  • Tracking the flow of financial data across the organisation in a controlled way, and integrating it for effective strategic decision making.
  • Creating the organisational structure.
  • General ledger accounting — chart of accounts, account groups, data transfer rules and general ledger accounts.
  • Tax and configuration.
  • Account payables.
  • Account receivables — customer master data and customer-related finance attributes such as account groups and payment terms.
  • Asset accounting.
  • Integration with sales and distribution, and materials management.

short.question: How is the management of hotels benefited by the use of a hotel management system?
short.answer:
A hotel management system runs hotels, hostels, lodges, suites, resorts and other rental properties efficiently. It handles day-to-day operations, administrative tasks, booking and billing, and helps guests be served well.

How it helps:

  • Booking and reservations are recorded in one place, so a room cannot be sold twice and availability is known at a glance.
  • Billing is produced accurately and quickly at checkout, with every charge on the guest's account already recorded.
  • Housekeeping is scheduled and tracked, so rooms are ready when guests arrive.
  • Guest history is kept, so returning guests are recognised and preferences honoured.
  • Reporting gives management a clear view of occupancy and revenue.
  • Banquet, HR, inventory and customer relationship management are all handled in the same system.

short.question: Write short notes on: (a) Payroll system (b) Weather forecasting system.
short.answer:
(a) Payroll system. Payroll is the process by which employers pay employees for work completed — salary and wages. A payroll management system is software that organises all the tasks connected with employee payment and tax filing.

It tracks the job done; calculates wages and salary; tracks attendance; records and manages leave; withholds taxes and deductions; prints and delivers cheques; completes direct deposits; and pays employment taxes to the government. In short it does the arithmetic and the paperwork that paying people involves.

(b) Weather forecasting system. A tool for predicting weather and climatic conditions at a future time for a given location — cloud cover, rain, snow, wind speed and temperature before they happen.

Forecasts are made by gathering as much data as possible about the current state of the atmosphere, particularly temperature, humidity and wind, then using meteorology to work out how it will evolve. Because the atmosphere is complex and not fully understood, forecasts grow less accurate the further ahead they look.

The main methods are: looking at current weather conditions; tracking the motion of air and clouds; finding previous weather patterns resembling current ones; examining changes in air pressure; and running computer models.

mcq.question: MS Word is an example of … software.
mcq.teacher_note: Word is application software — it does a job for you. System software (Windows) runs the machine; utility software maintains it.

mcq.question: What is the default file extension for all Word documents?
mcq.teacher_note: Since Word 2007 the default is .docx. The older .doc was used up to Word 2003.

mcq.question: How many ways can you save a document?
mcq.teacher_note: The book gives three: Save, Save As, and Save As with a different format.

mcq.question: Ctrl + Z is the keyboard shortcut for
mcq.teacher_note: Ctrl+Z is Undo. Redo is Ctrl+Y, paste is Ctrl+V.

mcq.question: The word wrap feature
options: Automatically moves text to the next line
Appears at the bottom of the document
Allows you to type over text
mcq.teacher_note: Word wrap is why you never press Enter at the end of a line — the text flows on by itself.

mcq.question: What does Ctrl + = do in MS Word?
mcq.teacher_note: Ctrl+= is subscript; Ctrl+Shift+= (with Shift, the key that goes up) is superscript.

mcq.question: How can you make the selected character superscripted?
mcq.teacher_note: The same rule: Shift lifts the character, so Shift gives superscript.

mcq.question: When typing in a word field manually, what must you press to insert the code's braces?
mcq.teacher_note: Ctrl+F9 inserts the field braces { }.

mcq.question: How many different documents can you open at one time?
options: As many as your computer memory will hold
As many as your taskbar can display
mcq.teacher_note: The limit is memory, not a number Word imposes.

mcq.question: Ctrl + B
mcq.teacher_note: B for bold. Each formatting shortcut matches its letter: B bold, I italic, U underline.

mcq.question: What is the default font used in an MS Word 2007 document?
mcq.teacher_note: Word 2007 introduced Calibri as the default, replacing Times New Roman.

mcq.question: Which of the following is not a type of page margin?
mcq.teacher_note: There are four margins — left, right, top and bottom. Centre is an alignment, not a margin.

mcq.question: Which would you choose to save a document with a new name?
mcq.teacher_note: Save keeps the same name; Save As gives you a new one — that is the whole difference between them.

mcq.question: Spreadsheet package is used to perform … operation.
mcq.teacher_note: A spreadsheet is built for calculation. Word processing is Word's job, presentations PowerPoint's.

mcq.question: .xlsx is the file extension of …
mcq.teacher_note: The three are easy to tell apart: .docx Word, .xlsx Excel, .pptx PowerPoint.

mcq.question: When all the numbers between 0 and 100 in a range should be displayed in red, apply
options: Use =IF() function to format the required numbers red
Apply Conditional Formatting command on Format menu
Select the cells that contain numbers between 0 and 100 then click red color on Text Color tool
mcq.teacher_note: Conditional formatting is exactly this: a rule that formats cells meeting a condition. Colouring them by hand would not follow the data if it changed.

mcq.question: In an Excel file, which of the following cannot be a sheet in a workbook?
mcq.teacher_note: A workbook holds worksheets, chart sheets and macro sheets. "Data sheet" is not one of them.

mcq.question: In Excel, which of the following is not a correct method of editing cell content?
mcq.teacher_note: F2, the formula bar and double-clicking all put you into edit mode. The Alt key only moves you around the ribbon.

mcq.question: Which of the following options is not available in the Paste Special dialog box?
mcq.teacher_note: Paste Special offers arithmetic operations — add, subtract, multiply, divide — but not the SQRT function.

mcq.question: The shortcut key Ctrl + R is used in Excel to
options: Right align the content of cell
Remove the cell contents of selected cells
Fill the selection with active cells to the right
mcq.teacher_note: In Excel Ctrl+R fills right. (In Word it right-aligns, which is the confusion to avoid — note the two programs differ.)

mcq.question: Which area in an Excel window allows entering values and formulas?
mcq.teacher_note: The formula bar shows the active cell's contents and is where you type and edit them.

mcq.question: .pptx is the file extension of …
mcq.teacher_note: The pattern holds across the suite: .docx Word, .xlsx Excel, .pptx PowerPoint.

mcq.question: MS PowerPoint is used to perform … operation.
mcq.teacher_note: PowerPoint builds slide shows. Calculation is Excel's job, writing Word's.

mcq.question: Which of the following statements is not true in PowerPoint?
options: You can type text directly into a PowerPoint slide but typing in a text box is more convenient
From Insert menu choose Picture and then File to insert your images into slides
You can view a PowerPoint presentation in Normal, Slide Sorter or Slide Show view
You can show or hide the task pane from View >> Toolbars
mcq.teacher_note: The other three are all true: text boxes are easier than typing straight onto a slide, pictures come from Insert, and there are exactly three main views. The task pane is controlled from the View tab, not from View » Toolbars.

mcq.question: To start or open Microsoft PowerPoint on your computer
options: Click Start > Programs > All Programs > Microsoft PowerPoint
Hit Ctrl + R then type ppoint.exe and Enter
Click Start > Run then type powerpnt then press Enter
mcq.teacher_note: All three start it: the Start menu, the Run box with ppoint.exe, and the Run box with powerpnt.

mcq.question: MS PowerPoint presentation is widely used as / for
mcq.teacher_note: All three are real uses. That breadth is why it is the standard presentation tool.

mcq.question: Which shortcut key inserts a new slide into the current presentation?
mcq.teacher_note: Ctrl+M inserts a slide. Ctrl+N creates a new presentation and Ctrl+S saves — worth keeping distinct.

mcq.question: From which menu can you access picture and chart?
mcq.teacher_note: Anything you bring into a slide — picture, chart, table, video, audio — comes from the Insert tab.

mcq.question: In a PowerPoint presentation
options: Sound clips can be inserted but not movie clips
Movie clips can be inserted but not sound clips
Both sound clips and movie clips cannot be inserted
Both sound clips and movie clips can be inserted
mcq.teacher_note: Both can be inserted. Options a, b and c each deny one or the other, so only d can be right.

mcq.question: … is not DBMS software.
mcq.teacher_note: Excel is a spreadsheet — it stores numbers in a grid, but it does not manage a database. Access, Oracle and MySQL all do. (Visual Basic is a programming language, not a DBMS either, but Excel is the answer the book gives.)

mcq.question: The extension of a database file in MS Access is …
mcq.teacher_note: Access files ended in .mdb; more recent versions use .accdb. Of the four, only MDB is a real Access extension — DBF belongs to dBase and FoxPro.

mcq.question: MS Access contains
mcq.teacher_note: All three, plus reports. Tables, queries, forms and reports are the four objects of an Access database.

mcq.question: Reports allow
options: Printing data based on queries and tables
mcq.teacher_note: Each object has one job: tables store, forms view and insert, queries ask, reports print.

mcq.question: An Access database file contains …
mcq.teacher_note: All of them, along with queries. An Access file holds more than the data itself.

mcq.question: A feature of the school management system is …
options: to keep student information and provide parent access
attendance, timetable management and teacher information
mcq.teacher_note: The system is deliberately broad: it covers students, parents, teachers, timetables, library, transport and hostel. All three statements are features of it.

mcq.question: Which is not included in an inventory management system?
options: Inventory management and inventory tracking and barcoding
Paying employment taxes to the government
mcq.teacher_note: Paying employment taxes belongs to the payroll system, not to inventory. The others are all standard inventory features.

mcq.question: Which is not included in a financial accounting system?
options: Tracking the flow of financial data across the organization
mcq.teacher_note: Booking, reservation and billing belong to the hotel management system. The other three are accounting functions.

mcq.question: Which is not a feature of a hotel management system?
options: Human resource and customer relationship management
Tracking the motion of air and clouds in the sky
mcq.teacher_note: Tracking air and clouds is a weather forecasting method. The rest are all hotel functions.

mcq.question: Which is a feature of a weather forecasting system?
options: Looking at current weather conditions and examining changes in air pressure
Tracking the motion of air and clouds in the sky
Finding previous weather patterns that resemble current ones
mcq.teacher_note: All three are among the methods listed, along with running computer models.

mcq.question: Which is not a domain-specific tool?
options: School, hotel and payroll management systems
Inventory management and financial accounting system
mcq.teacher_note: Watching TV is an activity, not software. Everything else named is an application built for one domain.

practical.question: Lab work — MS Word
practical.answer:
Work through these tasks in a word processor.

  1. Create a new document using any of the three methods and type three or four paragraphs, each of four or five sentences.
  2. Save the document using different methods, giving a different name each time.
  3. Close every open document, then reopen the three you created by three different methods.
  4. Delete two of them and rename the third to Computer.doc.
  5. Practise selecting a single word, a paragraph and a single line, using both the mouse and shortcut keys.
  6. Select the second paragraph: increase and decrease the font size, change the font, apply bold, italic and underline by mouse and by shortcut key, and justify the paragraph.
  7. Copy the second paragraph and paste it at the end of the document.
  8. Use cut on the second paragraph instead, and note the difference between cut and copy.
  9. Apply a drop cap to the first letter of each document, as in a newspaper.
  10. Format the first paragraph: a different font, justified, 14 points, blue text on a yellow background.
  11. Save that formatting as a style named "My Style", with Alt+1 as its shortcut.
  12. Apply "My Style" to the last paragraph.
  13. Modify the style: right align, double spacing, 6 points before and after. Rename it "MS Style" and apply it to the second paragraph.
  14. Open another document in another window and apply the style created in the first.
  15. Delete the "MS Style" style.
  16. Break the document into paragraphs, select them all and apply bullets or numbering.
  17. Insert a 5×5 table and then: insert a row above the third row, insert a column to the right of the second, and merge the last three rows.
  18. Move the table and resize it.
  19. Format the table with borders and shading: a ½-point double blue border and a yellow background.
  20. Using block arrows from AutoShapes, design a road sign for "Baneshwor Chowk".
  21. Use AutoCorrect to insert the word "Baneshwor" whenever you type "BC".
  22. Insert a header, a footer and page numbers.
  23. Insert clip art on each page and format the pictures properly.
  24. Prepare a main document for mailing to several recipients, create a data source holding their details, insert the merge fields, and view the finished documents.

practical.question: Project work — MS Word
practical.answer:
1. Prepare a one-month calendar using a table, with pictures inserted.
  2. Design a well-formatted newspaper page containing text, pictures and a drop cap.
  3. Design an attractive advertisement for admission to class 11 at your school.
  4. Create your résumé (bio-data) both with and without a template. It should contain your picture and a table.
  5. Use the equation editor's symbols to set out the mathematical equations you have been given.
  6. Create an attractive mark sheet along the lines of the BLE one.

practical.question: Lab work — MS PowerPoint
practical.answer:
1. Prepare at least five slides using design templates and the common formatting tools, presenting the generations of computers, the types of computer, memory units or processors.
  2. Use animation, automatic slide transition and transition styles to make those slides more attractive.
  3. Design a presentation showing an attractive place, the Himalaya or a temple in Nepal, with descriptions and background music.

practical.question: Project work — MS PowerPoint
practical.answer:
1. Create an attractive presentation showing the features of your college, university or locality.
  2. Embed an MS Excel sheet in MS PowerPoint, create a result sheet as in the spreadsheet task, and add a chart comparing student names with percentages.

teaching_plan.activity: Introduce the four applications and what each is for, and drill the four file extensions. Ask pupils which program they would open for a letter, a mark sheet, a talk and a list of students.
Demonstrate editing without retyping — break a paragraph and watch it reflow. Cover the three levels of formatting, then walk through mail merge in front of the class.
Cover workbook, worksheet, cell, range and active cell, then the four data types. Give pupils a sheet of their own to explore.
This is the idea that decides whether formulas work. Write =A1+B1 and copy it down, then repeat with $A$1, and let pupils see which answers move. Cover all three types in one demonstration.
Cover the four operator groups and the four rules for formulas, then work through SUM, AVERAGE, MAX, MIN, COUNT and SQRT on a real mark sheet.
Build an IF to grade a mark sheet, then nest two IFs. Follow with the components of a chart and have pupils chart the same data two ways.
Define slide, animation and transition, and hold the class to the distinction between the last two. Show all three views, then have pupils build five slides from a theme.
Cover the DBMS concept and the four Access objects, then the six domain-specific tools. For each, ask what job the software exists to do — that is what makes it domain-specific.
